name: Distribution Fit
description: Fit data to multiple distributions and rank by Goodness-of-Fit test
whenToUse: When it is unclear which distribution describes a measured characteristic: fits normal, lognormal, Weibull, exponential and further distributions to one numeric column and ranks them by goodness of fit; requires at least 5 values.
placeholderText: Select a data column and run the analysis to see results.
errMin5: At least 5 data points are required.
errGeneric: An error occurred during the analysis.
interpGood: Data is consistent with this distribution (p ≥ 0.10). Do not reject.
interpModerate: Borderline case (0.05 ≤ p < 0.10). Use with caution.
interpPoor: Distribution does not fit the data well (p < 0.05). Reject.
nddConfirmedText: All four tests pass at α = 0.05. The data is consistent with a normal distribution. Six Sigma tools like Cpk, control charts, and t-tests may be used without restriction.
nddBorderlineText: No test clearly rejects H₀, but at least one p-value is borderline. Normality is plausible but not conclusive. Larger sample or supplementary tests recommended.
nddMixedText: The tests disagree. Some reject normality, others do not. Check for outliers, sample size issues, or consider Box-Cox transformation.
nddRejectedText: The majority of tests reject H₀. The data is not normally distributed. Consider alternatives: Log-Normal, Weibull, or non-parametric methods.
nddSWDesc: Gold standard with highest statistical power. Compares order statistics with theoretical normal values.
nddADDesc: Especially sensitive in the distribution tails. Weights deviations at the extremes more heavily.
nddJBDesc: Asymptotic test based on skewness and kurtosis (χ² with 2 df). Reliable for large samples (n > 30).
nddDPDesc: Omnibus test: combines skewness and kurtosis Z-scores. Shows why normality fails.
nddTooSmall: Sample size too small for this test.
nddTooSmallJB: n < 8 — Jarque-Bera requires at least 8 data points.
nddTooSmallDP: n < 20 — D'Agostino-Pearson requires at least 20 data points.
